intro_html: Pillowy potato gnocchi in a cream soup loaded with turkey breast, spinach and a proper carrot, celery and onion base. This is the soup people order at the chain restaurant and then talk about for a week. Made at home in one pot, it comes in for less than the tip you would leave on that meal, and you get 14 of them.
cost_closing_html: About $2.79 a bowl for a cream soup with real turkey and real gnocchi in it. That is restaurant food at grocery store math.
shop_smart: Shelf-stable gnocchi is the cheap kind. It lives in the pasta aisle, not the refrigerated case, it keeps for months, and it cooks in about three minutes right in the broth.
Buy a frozen turkey breast roast and portion it. Turkey breast is at its cheapest around the holidays. Cook one, pull it, and freeze it in bags for soups like this one.
Heavy cream and milk together, not cream alone. Cutting the cream with milk keeps the soup silky, drops the cost, and drops the fat without anyone noticing.
Frozen chopped spinach goes in straight from the box. It costs less than fresh, it does not wilt into nothing, and there is no washing involved.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, celery and carrots small and sweat them in the olive oil in your big pot over medium heat until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add the minced garlic, the dried thyme and the Italian seasoning and stir for a minute until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring it to a simmer, and let the vegetables get fully tender.
Add the gnocchi and cook until they float and turn soft, only a few minutes. Do not walk away here.
Stir in the cooked turkey breast, the thawed chopped spinach, the heavy cream and the milk, then bring it back to a bare simmer without letting it boil.
Season with salt and black pepper and let it sit off the heat for a few minutes so it thickens up.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide what is left by 14 and ladle that exact weight into each container. Every bowl lands near 565 calories with 27 grams of protein. Reheat gently, because gnocchi and cream both prefer low and slow.
upsell_html: Chain restaurant soup for about $2.79 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

Add the garlic, thyme and Italian seasoning, then pour in the chicken broth.
